Case 2, corrected:

- \(n\equiv 1\pmod 3\) and \(n\equiv 3\pmod 7\): \(n=1+3k\), \(3k\equiv 2\pmod 7\), so \(k\equiv 3\pmod 7\), giving \(n\equiv 10\pmod{21}\).
- \(n\equiv 1\pmod 3\) and \(n\equiv 4\pmod 7\): \(n=1+3k\), \(3k\equiv 3\pmod 7\), so \(k\equiv 1\pmod 7\), giving \(n\equiv 4\pmod{21}\).

Case 3:

- \(n\equiv 2\pmod 3\) and \(n\equiv 2\pmod 7\): \(n\equiv 2\pmod{21}\).
- \(n\equiv 2\pmod 3\) and \(n\equiv 5\pmod 7\): \(n\equiv 5\pmod{21}\).

Thus valid residues modulo 21 are
\[
2,4,5,6,10,15.
\]

Since \(2011=21\cdot 95+16\), each residue \(1,\dots,16\) occurs \(96\) times among \(1\le n<2012\). All six valid residues are at most \(16\), so the count is
\[
6\cdot 96=576.
\]

\[
\boxed{576}
\]
